title: What Families Need: A Needs Assessment Within the Context of Family Centered Counseling
summary:
Background

Families of children with rare diseases often face unique challenges. The search for a diagnosis, coping with the condition in everyday life, and coordinating medical and social support services can place a considerable burden on parents and caregivers. To date, there is limited evidence regarding the types of support parents need and which aspects of counseling are most important to them.

Research Question

The aim of this study is to assess the needs and support preferences of parents and other primary caregivers of children with rare diseases. In addition, the study seeks to investigate how parents experience the counseling process and how satisfied they are with the information and support services provided.

Methods

This prospective observational study will include parents of children with rare diseases who participate in a counseling session. Participants will complete questionnaires at two time points. Prior to counseling, data on participants' expectations and baseline circumstances will be collected. With participants' informed consent, the counseling session will be audio recorded and subsequently analyzed for research purposes. Following the counseling session, participants will complete a second questionnaire assessing family needs as well as satisfaction with the counseling received. All collected data will be treated confidentially and used exclusively for scientific analysis.

interventions.name: Parents of children with rare diseases will be surveyed using standardized questionnaires before counseling at the Bonn Center for Rare Diseases and again after the counseling session.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
German speaking parents of children and young adults with a rare disease
Exclusion criteria:
Age below 18 years
Insufficient German language proficiency to participate in the survey and counseling session
Not being a parent or primary caregiver of a child or young adult with a rare disease
